| `Divider` | ✅ | A thematic break between two blocks of a page. An <hr>, so it carries role="separator" for free. | `orientation`: horizontal (default) | vertical. Vertical is self-stretch, so it runs the height of the tallest item in the flex row it sits in — it has no width of its own to give<br>`weight`: default (1px) | hairline (chrome/hairline, 0.5px). At 1px border/divider is already the lightest role there is (1.20:1) and the only way further down is thinner, not paler. | `DetailsToolbar` | ✅ | The action row under PageHeader on a record. 40 tall, one tab stop, a rule between EVERY adjacent item, and the overflow packed at the end. Folds container-relative: labels hide before icons, then items fold into the overflow from the right. | `groups`: DetailsToolbarGroup[] — { id, label, items }. `label` is role="group"'s name and IS the grouping; the separator is 1.31:1 and only its picture<br>`label`: role="toolbar"'s accessible name. Defaults to "Record actions"<br>`overflow`: { label?, expanded?, ref?, onSelect(foldedIds) } — the ⋯, sprung to the far end with ms-auto. Receives the ids that folded, so its menu can offer exactly those<br>`items[].menu`: the action opens a menu — draws the caret and sets aria-haspopup<br>`items[].disabled`: aria-disabled, NOT the disabled attribute: the item stays focusable and discoverable<br>`hidden`: take the bar off the page WITHOUT unmounting it. The action bar replaces the record's chrome, not just its title, so the toolbar steps aside with the header — otherwise 'Record Payment' is on screen twice meaning two different things. Hidden rather than unmounted because the bar holds the roving-tabindex position and its measured natural widths |
| `MiniList` | ✅ | The left column of a split view — a 353px panel with a toolbar that does not scroll and a listbox that does. A NAVIGATION control, not a list of links: selection drives a route and must never scroll the list or lose its position. Rows are a fixed 99 so long lists can be virtualised. | `label`: string — names the listbox<br>`items`: MiniListItem[] — { id, name, amount?, meta?, status?, statusVariant? }. `status` is the badge's text and `statusVariant` is which StatusBadge draws it. `meta` caps at three: past that it wraps and the row stops being 99<br>`activeId / onActivate`: the record being READ — the route<br>`selection`: { selected, onChange } — the records being ACTED ON. Present means checkboxes; ticking one must not navigate<br>`views / viewId / onViewChange`: the toolbar switcher<br>`onCreate`: the primary + in the toolbar<br>`moreEntries`: MenuEntry[] for the ⋯<br>`bar`: an <ActionBar density="compact"> while a bulk selection exists. It belongs on the same side as the checkboxes that filled it: the selection is a fact about THIS list, and putting its bar in the detail column makes the user look away from what they are ticking. PageChrome's three rules hold — the 56px cell never changes height, the toolbar is hidden rather than unmounted so the view switcher keeps its state, and there is no autoFocus anywhere (3.2.2 fires on every checkbox click) |
| `Nav` | ✅ | The left-hand navigation rail — a persistent, non-dismissible landmark holding a tree, in two widths. One per page. A parent discloses (<button>), a leaf navigates (<a>); collapsing changes the width, not the sequence. | `items`: NavNode[] — { id, label, href?, icon?, badge?, action?, children? }<br>`sections`: { header, items }[] — a titled group<br>`currentId`: string — the ONE aria-current="page"; ancestors are derived<br>`collapsed / onCollapsedChange`: boolean / (next) => void<br>`product`: { name, mark? } — the brand band, which deliberately does not flip<br>`footer`: ReactNode — content at the foot of the rail, above the collapse bar (a build note). Expanded rail only<br>`label`: string (default "Main") — the landmark name |
| `PageChrome` | ✅ | The cell a PageHeader and an ActionBar share. One fixed block-size equal to the taller (64 vs 48), the header hidden rather than unmounted so it keeps its state, and no autoFocus anywhere — focus must not cross the swap. | `children`: the <PageHeader>. Always rendered; hidden while `bar` is present<br>`bar`: the <ActionBar>, or nothing. Present means a selection exists |
| `PageHeader` | ✅ | The 64px band at the top of the content column — the page's <h1>, its context and its actions. Three page types as a discriminated union: list (the title is a view-switcher menu button), create, detail (back + parent link). NOT a second banner: place it inside <main>; the top bar owns that landmark. | `type`: 'list' | 'create' | 'detail' — a discriminated union, not three options on one shape. A detail without `parent` does not compile<br>`title`: string — the page's only <h1>. On `list` it lives inside the switcher button<br>`views / onViewChange / viewMenuOpen / onViewMenuToggle`: list only — the switcher renders a real listbox, because aria-expanded over nothing is 4.1.2<br>`parent / onBack`: detail only — { label, href }, rendered as a LINK above the h1, never an <h2><br>`actions`: HeaderAction[] — { id, label, icon, disabled?, onSelect }. No Count cap<br>`cta`: { label, icon?, disabled?, onSelect } — optional, at most one |
| `SettingsBar` | ✅ | The bar at the top of the settings area. It REPLACES TopBar for as long as the user is in settings — it is never stacked beneath it. Owns the scroll region the sticky bar needs. | `title`: the settings area's <h1>. Truncates, with the full string kept in the title attribute<br>`mark`: the product's own logo as a node (an instance swap in Figma). A brand asset: not a ZF icon, never recoloured<br>`showSearch / showClose`: both optional; the bar still names where you are without them<br>`onSearch / onClose`: onClose also fires on Escape, guarded so it does not fire from inside the search<br>`children`: the settings content that scrolls under the bar |
| `SettingsShell` | ✅ | Settings level 1 — the bar across the top, the SettingsNav rail on the left and the chosen settings page in the body, separated by a 2px gutter. | `sections / currentId / onNavigate`: passed straight to SettingsNav<br>`onBack`: returns to level 0. The rail unmounts and the bar's left slot reverts to the title<br>`header / footer`: grid rows OUTSIDE the scroller, so a page header needs no sticky at all<br>`children`: the scrolling body content |
| `SplitView` | ✅ | The two-column detail view — a MiniList on the left, the record it points at on the right. Each column scrolls on its own; neither scrolls the other. | `list`: the left column — a <MiniList>. Owns its own width and its own edge<br>`children`: the record. Gets min-w-0 and its own scroller |
| `Tabs` | ✅ | One record, several views of it. A 40px strip with a 2px selected indicator, one tab stop, and a trailing slot on the same baseline for a control that acts on whichever tab is open. | `items`: TabItem[] — { id, label, badge?, disabled? }. A disabled tab is SKIPPED by the arrows, not focused-and-inert: a tab is a destination, and arrowing onto one you cannot open is a dead end<br>`value / onChange`: controlled. Selection follows focus, which is the APG default for a panel that is cheap to render<br>`label`: names the tablist. Required<br>`trailing`: a control on the strip's baseline — a Segmented view switch, a filter. Outside the arrow-key model on purpose: it is not a tab<br>`children`: the panel. One node; the caller decides what the active tab renders<br>`inset`: section (default, space/15 = 30 — for a card that is pad={0} so the strip's rule can reach its edges) | none (flush — for a container that has already inset its content). At `section` inside a creation-page body the tabs sat 30 further in than the form labels above them and the shared baseline started in the wrong place. |
| `TopBar` | ✅ | The application top bar — a 48px dark chrome strip with the product lockup, a scoped search field and a right-hand account cluster. One banner per document. If it is about the current page it does not belong here (§7). | `product`: { name, mark, wordmark?, href? }<br>`search`: { scope, value, onValueChange, onSubmit, onScopeOpen, scopeOpen? } — one object, not five props<br>`org`: { name, onOpen, open? } — optional<br>`actions`: TopBarAction[] — { id, label, icon, filled?, onSelect }<br>`account`: { name, initials, onOpen, open? }<br>`apps`: { onOpen, open? } |
| `Wizard` | ✅ | A stepper — where the user is in a multi-step flow. Three orientations from one steps array; Figma’s two step atoms are collapsed into one presentation variant. | `steps`: Step[] — { id, label, description?, state, clickable? }. `description` is a second line under the label and works in BOTH orientations. It costs two alignment fixes, both invisible until a description exists and then wrong everywhere: the label centres against the marker inside its own 24-tall line box rather than against the two-line block, and the connector is pinned to the marker's centre (mt-6, half the marker) rather than riding items-center on the row — which is the same place ONLY while every step is exactly one marker tall.<br>`orientation`: `horizontal` · `vertical` · `tabs`<br>`onStepClick`: (id: string) => void<br>`label`: string — REQUIRED; an unlabelled <ol> of steps announces as a bare list |

## Feedback

| Component | | Use it when | Props |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Banner` | ✅ | One line saying what just happened, at the top of the thing it happened to. | `tone`: danger | warning | success | info (default). Each gets its own SHAPE as well as its own colour<br>`children`: the message. One line<br>`onDismiss`: renders the ✕ at 24 — the glyph is 16 and 2.5.8 asks for 24. Omit for a banner the user cannot get rid of |
| `Progress` | ✅ | A determinate progress bar — how far along a thing is, as a fraction. Introduced by ZF-UPLOAD.md §11 as a system primitive so the next component that needs one does not draw a second. | `value`: 0-100, clamped — a caller dividing by a zero total should not paint outside the track<br>`label`: REQUIRED. Names what is progressing ("Uploading receipt-08.pdf"), never "Progress"<br>`tone`: `default` · `success` · `danger` |

## Overlays

| Component | | Use it when | Props |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ColumnConfig` | ✅ | Which columns a table shows and in what order. A Modal holding a draft list: checkbox = visible, drag handle or arrow keys = order, Save commits and Close discards. | `open / onClose`: controlled. onClose discards the draft<br>`items`: ColumnConfigItem[] — { id, label, visible, locked? }. `locked` cannot be hidden or moved<br>`onSave`: (next) => void. The dialog does not close itself<br>`title`: defaults to 'Rearrange the Columns' |
| `Menu` | ✅ | A floating list of commands, anchored to whatever opened it, with sub-menus. NOTHING in zf-design-cannon.md measures a dropdown menu — §2.15 Popover is a coach mark with a Nose pointer — so every value is borrowed from a measured neighbour and cited in the source, never invented. | `anchor`: HTMLElement | null — the element it hangs off. Focus returns here on Escape<br>`open / onClose`: controlled<br>`items`: MenuNode[] — { id, label, icon?, children?, onSelect?, disabled?, separatorBefore? }. `children` and `onSelect` are mutually exclusive: a branch is not a command<br>`label`: string — REQUIRED. A role=menu with no name announces as 'menu'<br>`align`: start | end (default). Which edge of the panel lines up with the anchor's. `end` is right for every ⋯ in the system; `start` is right for a trigger on the LEFT, where `end` would throw a 240px panel backwards across its own button. The viewport clamp applies either way<br>`emphasis`: default | strong. `strong` accents the glyphs at rest (primary/default, 4.32 — 1.4.11 asks a graphic for 3:1) and fills the row under the pointer, label and glyph moving with it. The fill is the {family}/HOVER role, never /default: white on primary/default is 4.32 and fails 1.4.3's 4.5 for the 13px label on it, where primary/hover is 5.48 L / 8.62 D. A DANGER row fills danger/hover with danger/on-danger — 7.04 L / 8.26 D — so the one row that destroys something never answers the pointer in the same colour as the rest. Also widens the icon-to-label gap 8 -> 12 |
| `Modal` | ✅ | The dialog you DO something in — a form, a table, a wizard step. Three regions (header 56, body, footer 72), four widths, flush to the top edge with square top corners, actions on the body's own left margin, and the body is the only scroller. A native <dialog> opened with showModal(). | `open / onRequestClose`: controlled. RETURN FALSE TO VETO — §5: 'onClose says it happened, onRequestClose says it was asked for', and a dialog that cannot refuse cannot protect a half-filled form<br>`title`: string — REQUIRED, the visible <h2> and the accessible name via aria-labelledby<br>`width`: 'sm' | 'md' | 'lg' | 'xl' — 500 / 600 / 700 / 900<br>`children`: the body, the only thing that scrolls<br>`primaryAction / secondaryAction`: { label, onSelect, disabled? }<br>`showClose`: hiding it obliges a labelled dismiss in the footer — 2.1.2<br>`inset`: away from the top edge, which rounds all four corners |
| `SidePanel` | ✅ | A right-hand drawer — supporting detail or a focused task beside the main content. Built on <dialog>, so the scrim, focus trap, Esc, inert page and focus return are native. If the user must answer before continuing it is a modal, not this (§7). | `open / onClose`: boolean / () => void<br>`title`: string — names the dialog via aria-labelledby, and the close button<br>`children`: ReactNode — Figma’s Body INSTANCE_SWAP; the scroll container<br>`footer`: ReactNode — omit for Figma’s Footer=none<br>`showClose`: boolean (default true)<br>`tintedHeader`: boolean — a 1.12:1 change; §11 decision 3<br>`modal`: boolean (default true) — false uses show(): no trap, no scrim |

## Patterns — composed blocks

| Component | | Use it when | Props |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `SettingsNav` | ✅ | The settings rail at level 1 — the same links the SettingsPage cards hold, folded into a two-level disclosure tree in a 240px panel. | `sections`: SettingsNavSection[] -> groups -> children. THE SAME array SettingsPage renders as cards (§8.1); if the two ever disagree the user has found a bug<br>`currentId`: the leaf id for the current route. The open branch is DERIVED from it, not from a click, so a deep link finds its group already open<br>`onNavigate`: called with the leaf. Omit to let the <a href> navigate |
| `SettingsPage` | ✅ | The settings directory — every settings destination in the product, grouped into cards and colour-coded by category. The default landing page for the settings area, rendered inside SettingsBar. | `sections`: SettingsSection[] -> cards -> groups -> links. Section title is an h2, group title an h3, links a real <ul> of <a href><br>`query`: filters IN PLACE. Empty groups, cards and sections drop out; the match covers the group title as well as the link labels<br>`tone`: per group: blue | green | orange | red, mapped to chart/1, /4, /5, /7 |
